KJFB20/21/30/31 refers to a specific set of SKS (Sundhedsvæsenets Klassifikations System) codes used within the Danish healthcare system to classify particular surgical procedures. These codes are highly significant in the context of national quality monitoring because they define the operations—specifically ileocecal resection and right-sided hemicolectomy, including their laparoscopic variants—that form the numerator for [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] [^src1]. 

Indikator 3 is a quality indicator within the Danish Quality Database for Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (DANIBD) that tracks the rate of postoperative colonoscopies following ileocecal resection in patients with Crohn's disease [^src1]. By relying on the KJFB20/21/30/31 codes, the database ensures the precise and standardized inclusion of relevant surgical operations in this quality measurement, preventing data drift and allowing for accurate evaluation of postoperative care practices across regions [^src1]. 

The formal use of these codes is tied directly to the rollout of the indicator itself. On October 1, 2022, Indikator 3 was officially entered into the national registry system, and the KJFB20/21/30/31 codes (alongside the KUJF32/35 codes) were actively applied for patient registration and data tracking [^src1]. This implementation was part of a broader initiative to establish rigorous, standardized quality measurements for IBD care in Denmark [^src1].
